title: Collection Anatomy and Distribution
objective: Package plugins, modules, roles, docs, and metadata under an FQCN.

sourceAlignment.title: Ansible for DevOps, 2nd Edition
sourceAlignment.author: Jeff Geerling
sourceAlignment.note: Original Code Forge companion material; no book prose is reproduced.

paragraphs: A collection uses namespace.name identity and a galaxy.yml manifest. Its plugins and roles live in conventional paths, and documentation and tests travel with the implementation.
Build artifacts can be published to Galaxy or Automation Hub. Consumers use FQCNs and bounded version constraints, while configured collection paths determine installation discovery.
explanation.rule: Operational rule: Package plugins, modules, roles, docs, and metadata under an FQCN.

examples.title: Working design artifact
examples.code:
collection:
  namespace: codeforge
  name: training
  manifest: galaxy.yml
  fqcn: codeforge.training.example
  versioned: true
examples.note: Use this as a reasoning model before applying changes to the disposable lab.
